newsitem.title: UK: Wet Brent trades lower again, Forties, Ekofisk sli.
newsitem.headline: Wet Brent trades lower again, Forties, Ekofisk sli.

text.p: North Sea crudes retreated in modest trade on Monday with buyer resistance encouraged by a falling screen helping pressure differentials, traders said.
Feb 18-20 Brent traded twice at Mar Brent +5 cents after other cargoes fetched premiums of 15-25 cents on Friday, and traders said it could slide further.
Two Ekofisks for end-Feburary were done around five cents easier at Dated Brent +30 cents. A Forties loading March 2-7 traded around five cents easier at Dated Brent +43.
An Oseberg fetched Dated Brent +36 cents a barrel, down from trade at +50 cents last Wednesday.
March IPE Brent fell below $21 a barrel to trade 21 cents down at $20.74, its lowest for six months, at $17.52 GMT.
The sole cargo nominated for Monday was kept by BP ahead of the five o'clock deadline.
Intermonth spreads were broadly steady, with Mar/Apr trading at +34, +35 and +37 cents and Apr/May talked at +30/+33 cents. There was unconfirmed talk of Feb/Mar trade at +20 cents.
Brent Contracts for Differences were mostly easier. This week was talked two cents lower at +0.03/0.05 and next week four cents lower at -0.10/-0.08. Feb 24-28 was unchanged at +0.18/0.20.
In the Mediterranean, the market for sour crudes looked softer, with plentiful supplies and local refiners complaining of poor margins.
While a large Urals cargo loading mid-Feb traded on Friday at Dated Brent -73 cents, traders said that the market was now talked in the Dated Brent -80s or even -90s.

"I think that was a particular deal. (The seller) was probably had a short at even higher numbers and paid up," said one trader. Traders noted differentials for small and large cargoes were divided by freight rates, with smaller vessels suffering from high shipping costs.
